You are going to redraw one layout sheet for our iGEM team wiki (page: Human Practices Industry Engagement and Support). Draw it on your own without asking me anything.

ATTACHED
- 00-style.png = STYLE REFERENCE: top, our team's own hand-cut paper illustration; bottom, props already drawn for the site. Copy technique, textures and palette. Do not copy their objects or composition.
- IN1.png = LAYOUT SHEET: grey stand-ins on a plain light background showing where each object goes and its rough shape. The small number in the top-left corner is only the sheet number.

TASK
Make ONE new image that can be laid exactly over the layout sheet:
1. Same canvas: 1536 x 1024 pixels, landscape.
2. Same objects in the same places, at the same sizes, with the same outlines. Do not add, remove, merge, swap, turn or move any object. Keep the empty space between objects; no object may touch another.
3. Redraw every object in the style described below. The grey layout sheet only shows placement and rough shapes; it is a stand-in, do not copy its flat look.
4. Background: fully transparent (PNG with alpha). If transparency is impossible, use one perfectly flat pure white #FFFFFF background with nothing else on it.
5. Do not draw the sheet number. No text, letters, numbers, labels, logos, borders, frames, ground lines, floors or shadows anywhere.

STYLE (match 00-style.png: our homepage art on top, our existing props below)
- Flat hand-cut paper collage: every shape is cut from matte coloured paper with scissors, so its edges are straight, slightly irregular cuts with a few corners. No outlines, no ink lines.
- Each shape is one flat paper colour. Sides and details are separate overlapping pieces of slightly darker or lighter paper. Very light volume as in the existing props, but no gradients, no airbrush, no glossy highlights, no 3D rendering, no drop shadows.
- Texture as in the reference: oil-pastel or crayon scratches in a second, warmer colour running in one direction across each piece, a few dry-brush streaks, fine dark speckles and visible paper grain. Soil is speckled and dotted with small pale stones.
- Simple, chunky, readable shapes. It must look like the same artist as the props in the bottom half of 00-style.png (envelope, speech bubbles, blackboard, field plot).
- Palette, muted like the reference (never pure white, never black, never neon): olive #7B7639, dark olive #58542A, ochre #C88F35, mustard #B58D3A, rust #83403C, plum #6E4764, mauve #8D6B84, pale mauve #B59BB8, lilac #9479B8, orange #E88F46, amber #DFA340, cream #E6D7BB.

OBJECTS on sheet IN1 (IN1.png)
  a) top row, 1 from left: a closed envelope, the same object and colours as the closed envelope in the bottom half of 00-style.png, redrawn larger with the same cream paper, ochre scratches and olive and mauve torn pieces along the bottom.
  b) top row, 2 from left: the same envelope opened, its triangular flap up, the same as the open envelope in the bottom half of 00-style.png, redrawn larger.
  c) top row, 3 from left: an invitation card coming out of an envelope: a cream card with a second slightly darker card behind it, a round ochre seal near the top, four short olive and mustard bars for lines of writing, a mauve torn corner.
  d) middle row, 1 from left: a meeting table seen slightly from the front: rust table top and legs with a plum front edge, two cream papers and two cream cups on it, and one simple faceless paper pawn on each side (olive on the left, mauve on the right) facing each other.
  e) middle row, 2 from left: presentation materials: a small rust easel board with a cream sheet showing a simple diagram (an olive circle, a rust arrow, three amber, mustard and ochre colour swatches and two mauve bars), and a mustard booklet leaning against its right leg.
  f) bottom row, 1 from left: a cream speech bubble with its tail at the bottom right, showing one olive leaf and three small plum dots, an olive torn corner.
  g) bottom row, 2 from left: a slightly darker cream speech bubble with its tail at the bottom left, showing three small amber, mustard and ochre swatches above one mauve bar, a mauve torn corner.

These are decorative illustrations only: no logos, no brand names, no text, no real people; any figures are simple faceless paper pawns.
If the result is not usable, I will reply "重画 IN1"; then draw it again with the same rules.
